priya: quick heads-up — I pushed a small A100 vs H100 bench across eu-west1 / us-east1 / asia-south1 for mistral-7b, mosaic-7b, llama2-7b. TL;DR: H100 wins tokens/sec by ~20-35% in decode heavy runs but prefill p99 varies by kernel and ctx. details below.

bench-bot: auto-summary attached (prefill p50/p99, decode tok/s, $/1M tokens). CSV uploaded to S3: s3://bench-results/3456789012/summary.csv :mag_right:

sam: raw highlights I looked at:
- mistral-7b (ctx=2048, q8x4): H100 eu-west1 decode=2200 tok/s, a100 decode=1700 tok/s. prefill p99: H100=48ms, A100=72ms.
- mosaic-7b (ctx=1024, q4_0): H100 decode=2500, A100=1850. prefill p99 gap smaller (~15ms).
- llama2-7b (ctx=4096): long prefill on H100 gets worse for flash-attn2 when >3k tokens, fallback to triton reduces p99.

ana: kernel observation: flash-attn2 on H100 gives best steady-state decode but we've seen higher prefill p99 at long ctx (KV cache warmup pattern). on A100, our custom triton kernels sometimes beat flash for prefill slices <512. so kernel choice is region+ctx dependent.

elaine: quick cost math I ran (on-demand GPU rates + avg util):
- H100 decode-heavy: ~ $8.2 / 1M tokens (assumes 75% decode share, 90% util).
- A100 balanced: ~ $6.1 / 1M tokens (but if decode dominates + high kv-hit, H100 ROI improves).
If KV cache hit >=70% the per-token prefill cost drops and A100 gets relatively cheaper for mixed traffic.

mike: ops note: in asia-south1 we observed thermal fallback on one H100 pod under sustained 900 tok/s for 30s — autoscaler did swap to a diff instance class. might affect p99 in prod if we pack too tightly. :warning:

priya: sounds good. next steps: run longer-tail tests (10m steady-state) with q8x4 and q4_0, force kernel combos and record prefill p50/p99 + decode tok/s + cost calc. want regional breakdown & reserved vs on-demand delta.
